a: **Force** is a push or pull on an object. Formula: F = ma (Force = mass × acceleration). Unit: Newton (N). 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².
**Newton's 1st Law (Inertia):** An object stays at rest or moves in a straight line at constant speed unless a net force acts on it.
**Newton's 2nd Law:** F = ma. Net force equals mass times acceleration. Direction of F is the direction of a.
**Newton's 3rd Law:** For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Forces come in pairs.
**Kinetic energy:** KE = ½ mv². Unit: Joule (J). m = mass (kg), v = speed (m/s).
**Gravitational potential energy:** PE = mgh. m = mass, g ≈ 9.8 m/s², h = height above reference.
**Ohm's law:** V = IR. Voltage (V) = Current (A) × Resistance (Ω).
**Power:** P = VI = I²R = V²/R. Also P = W/t (work over time). Unit: Watt (W).
**Velocity** is speed with direction (m/s). **Acceleration** is rate of change of velocity (m/s²). a = (v − u) / t.
**Wave speed:** v = fλ. v = speed, f = frequency (Hz), λ = wavelength (m).
**Density:** ρ = m / V. Mass over volume. Unit: kg/m³ (or g/cm³).
**Pressure:** P = F / A. Force over area. Unit: Pascal (Pa) = N/m².
**Work:** W = Fd cosθ. Work done by a force equals change in kinetic energy (work–energy theorem).
**Momentum:** p = mv. Unit: kg·m/s. Conservation: total momentum before = total after (if no external force).
**Snell's law:** n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Relates angles of incidence and refraction at a boundary.
